semantic_correction.stem: A client who uses an insulin pump is preparing for air travel. Which statement shows correct understanding of insulin and pump-supply planning?

options.A: I will keep insulin and pump supplies in my carry-on, protect insulin from temperature extremes, and bring extra supplies for delays.
options.B: I will put insulin and pump supplies in checked baggage because the cargo area provides reliable medication storage.
options.C: I will place insulin directly against frozen ice packs because freezing does not reduce insulin effectiveness.
options.D: I will bring the exact planned amount of insulin and supplies because travel delays do not change my needs.

semantic_correction.rationale: FDA insulin-pump travel guidance says to pack pump supplies, including insulin, in carry-on luggage because checked baggage may be delayed, lost, or broken. FDA also advises travelers to bring enough medication and equipment for potential delays and to review medication storage requirements. Separate FDA insulin-storage guidance warns that extreme temperatures reduce insulin effectiveness, advises keeping insulin as cool as possible without freezing it, and states that frozen insulin should not be used. Therefore option A combines the appropriate travel and storage precautions.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When traveling with insulin-pump therapy, keep insulin and pump supplies in carry-on luggage, protect insulin from temperature extremes and freezing, and plan extra medication/supplies for possible delays.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'all'/'only' distractor cueing, integrated the current FDA carry-on, delay-planning, and temperature-protection instructions into one concise travel decision, and balanced all four alternatives.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original concept was valid but included absolute distractors. The revised item uses current FDA travel and storage guidance with parallel planning statements.

option_audit.A: Correct. It applies FDA carry-on, extra-supply, and temperature-protection guidance.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. FDA specifically advises against checked baggage for pump supplies because it can be delayed, lost, or broken.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. FDA states that insulin should not be frozen and frozen insulin should not be used.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. FDA advises planning enough medication and equipment for potential travel delays.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone contains all three source-supported travel-safety elements.
cueing_check: All four choices are first-person travel plans of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
